correctness.rationale: Scaling each power-mesh cell gives the exact distributional identity Q_n-I=n^{-q}sum_{j<=n}Z_j, with independent centered Z_j and explicit integrated variance. For 0<alpha<1/2, v_j~(alpha^2p^4/12)j^{2q-4}; the derivative/width Taylor remainder is uniformly lower order on j>=2. When q<3/2 the independent series converges in L2 and almost surely. Only its first term has the unbounded power right tail P(Z_1>x)~x^{-1/alpha}; the remainder is sub-Gaussian by Hoeffding with square-summable bounds, giving the exact tail equivalence. At q=3/2 variance grows c log n and at q>3/2 it grows c n^(2q-3)/(2q-3), with Lindeberg since bounded later summands are negligible relative to the normalization. Differentiating c/(2q-3) finds p*=2/(1-alpha). Independently exact-rational cell variance calculations verified v_j=3/4 for alpha=1/3,p=3 and v_j=2(6j^2-6j+1)/9 for alpha=1/4,p=4 for all j=1..30.
